case_analysis.thread_summary: The thread covers the final stage of a Bluetooth SIG product qualification submission managed by a consultant on behalf of a member company. The customer reviews and approves the qualification submission details before final submission. A qualification workspace review identified policy-related constraints under the newer Bluetooth qualification process. After submission, the case moves into Bluetooth SIG review, followed by preparation of the compliance folder documentation.
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: The product is intended to operate as an LE-only product at the application level, but the referenced Bluetooth design is qualified as a dual-mode implementation. Under the newer qualification process, changing the registered ICS from dual-mode to single-mode would trigger inter-layer consistency check failures when the included QDIDs/designs are dual-mode. The consultant therefore keeps the registration as dual-mode while relying on software to disable BR/EDR functionality in the shipped product. The submission also contains a TCW-related warning because the referenced qualification was created using older ICS definitions that do not fully align with current consistency-check requirements. The submission proceeds with a TCW review by Bluetooth SIG.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: The consultant's decision is driven by qualification-tool consistency rules rather than by the product's marketed operating mode. Because the included qualified design is dual-mode, modifying the registration to a single-mode ICS would block submission. Maintaining the dual-mode registration while disabling BR/EDR in software preserves consistency with the referenced qualification data and allows the submission to pass the qualification workflow, subject to TCW review.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: If the registration were altered to an LE-only ICS despite relying on a dual-mode referenced design, the submission could fail consistency checks and be unable to proceed to formal qualification. Incorrect handling of the TCW condition could also delay Bluetooth SIG approval and completion of the qualification process. Additional rework of qualification data, documentation, or registration structure could result.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When reusing existing Bluetooth qualified designs under the post-QPRDv3 qualification process, qualification decisions must follow the structure and constraints of the referenced design data. If a referenced design is dual-mode, attempts to force a single-mode registration can trigger consistency-check failures, so consultants should evaluate ICS dependencies and TCW implications before changing transport declarations.
